author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The arrival of the rainy season in Sudan’s Blue Nile region is worsening already dire conditions for thousands of displaced people living in camps such as Elcarama in the city of Damazine.

Families who have fled renewed fighting between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces say they are facing severe shortages of clean water, food, and shelter. Many of those arriving in recent weeks have escaped escalating violence in southern parts of Blue Nile State.

The United Nations says more than 50,000 people were displaced between April and May alone, with numbers continuing to rise as the conflict spreads. While some are staying in overcrowded camps, others remain in makeshift shelters or are exposed to the elements.

title: Sudan: Rainy season worsens displacement crisis in Blue Nile as conflict spreads

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The United Nations says more than 390,000 people have crossed from Lebanon into Syria since Israeli bombardments began in March, with tens of thousands returning in the past month alone.

Many of those returning had originally fled Syria during the rule of former President Bashar al-Assad. Following the collapse of his government in late 2024, Syrians have increasingly begun returning home as security conditions gradually stabilize.

But UN officials warn that humanitarian funding is falling far short of what is needed to support the growing number of returnees. The UN says it has received only a fraction of the billions required this year to assist millions of Syrians in need of aid.

Humanitarian agencies have already been forced to reduce emergency food assistance and suspend major support programs, including bread subsidies relied upon by millions. The situation is also being worsened by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which has pushed up food and fuel prices across the regio
title: UN warns Syria aid crisis worsening as refugees return amid regional instability

description:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to extend their ceasefire by an additional 45 days following talks between officials in Washington, DC, aimed at preventing a wider regional escalation.

Despite the extension, Israeli strikes and evacuation orders have continued in southern Lebanon, where residents say daily life remains disrupted by ongoing military activity. Since the ceasefire began in April, hundreds of people have reportedly been killed in Israeli strikes across Lebanon.

Meanwhile in Gaza, Israeli forces say they carried out a strike targeting a senior Hamas official in Gaza City. Palestinian officials report that at least seven people were killed and dozens wounded after attacks hit residential areas west of the city.

The latest developments come as diplomats push for continued negotiations, while concerns grow over repeated ceasefire violations and the risk of renewed broader conflict across the region.

description:
Political uncertainty is growing in the United Kingdom as pressure mounts on Prime Minister Keir Starmer following major Labour Party losses in local elections.
Attention is increasingly turning toward Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham, a popular figure within Labour who is now being discussed as a possible successor. Speculation intensified after Labour MP Josh Simons resigned his seat, potentially opening a path for Burnham to enter Parliament and challenge Starmer’s leadership.
The situation comes as Reform UK gains momentum in several areas once considered Labour strongholds, raising concerns about the party’s electoral future. Meanwhile, financial markets are reacting nervously to the political instability, with the pound weakening and borrowing costs rising.
Starmer is also facing growing dissent within his own party, with dozens of Labour MPs reportedly calling for him to step aside as the government struggles to address economic pressures linked to the fallout from the war
